summary: Abhay Bhushan's reply to Bob Braden's comments on FTP in RFC 430. He agrees that most should go into the forthcoming official specification, and answers them one by one, in preparation for the March 16 FTP meeting at BBN. It is a discussion paper.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC responds to proposed changes to FTP. It records which suggestions the author supports and which issues he thinks need more discussion.

subtitle: Abhay Bhushan's response to comments on the evolving FTP specification.

tldr.problem: Comments on RFC 430 raised design questions for the forthcoming official FTP specification.
tldr.mechanism: Abhay Bhushan responds to specific items, supports several suggestions, and raises additional topics for discussion.
tldr.outcome: The RFC prepares discussion for an upcoming FTP meeting; it is a set of comments, not a final specification.

sections.title: Response to FTP Comments
sections.content: Abhay Bhushan says most of Bob Braden's comments in RFC 430 are useful suggestions for the forthcoming official FTP specification. He writes this response and additional views to inform discussion at an FTP meeting announced for March 16 at BBN.
sections.plainLanguage: Bhushan reviews suggestions for changing FTP. He agrees that most are useful and should be considered for the upcoming specification.

sections.title: Commands, Replies, and Data Parameters
sections.content:
Bhushan supports bit-flag coding for descriptors and says command-reply sequencing should be tightened so programs can use FTP conveniently. He argues that a server should send a 300 greeting before accepting commands.

He discusses alternatives for encoding FTP parameters, supports considering the GSOC command, and suggests that multiple data-transfer parameters might be sent in one command line.
sections.plainLanguage: Programs need predictable replies and a clear point when they can start sending commands. The note also considers ways to express transfer settings and establish data connections.

sections.title: Mail and Site-Specific Questions
sections.content:
The RFC says site-dependent FTP parameters need more discussion. It also lists open mail questions: sending to multiple users, standard user names, consistent sender and date information, and handling bulk mail.

For bulk mail, the author raises the possibility of placing a file in the user's directory and notifying the user, rather than printing all the material on the console.
sections.plainLanguage: The author asks for more discussion about FTP differences between sites. He also lists unresolved choices about recipients, sender details, and bulk mail.

references.text: Braden, R., "Comments on RFC 430", RFC 430, February 1973.
